content:
British actor Robert Pattinson has been named the next James Bond, ending years of speculation and secrecy about the future of the beloved spy thriller series.

“James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime,” he said in a statement released Monday by Amazon MGM Studios. “To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement.”

Pattinson, 40, was chosen from a handful of actors who made the shortlist to replace Daniel Craig as 007. They reportedly included Callum Turner, Jack Lowden, Josh O’Connor and Nicholas Hoult.

With his selection, he becomes the seventh actor to be cast as the British Secret Intelligence Service agent since the film series’ 1962 debut with actor Sean Connery in “Dr. No.”

“He has the timeless soul of 007 and brings a completely new spirit,” said Denis Villeneuve, who will direct the franchise’s 26th installment.

Mike Hopkins, head of Prime Video and Amazon MGM Studios, also credited Pattinson’s “remarkable range, magnetic screen presence, and quiet intensity” for making him the best choice.

Pattinson’s screen time includes his starring role as Batman in the 2022 “The Batman” and in the yet-to-be-released sequel, “The Batman: Part II.” He most recently starred as journalist Chris Hansen in the psychological thriller “Primetime.” He’s also commonly known for his role in the “Twilight” series.

A 26-second sneak peek clip released with Monday’s announcement shows Pattinson as Bond emerging from the dark while intensely looking past the barrel of a gun he’s holding and wearing the iconic character’s black-and-white suit. It appears to reference Bond’s death at the end of the 2021 film “No Time to Die,” stating: “James Bond Will Return.”

The movie will be the first Bond film undertaken by Amazon MGM Studios, after Amazon purchased MGM in 2022 for $8.5 billion.

The purchase ignited concerns that the colossal corporation, owned by billionaire Jeff Bezos, would dilute the Bond movies’ worth with spinoffs and streaming deals.
